facts.fact: On a theatrical feature the producer must give the director ten weeks, or one day of editing for each two days of scheduled photography, whichever is longer, to complete the Director's Cut.

value.ratio: 1 editing day per 2 scheduled shooting days

facts.fact: On a High Budget SVOD picture of 96 minutes or longer budgeted at $22,500,000 or more, the Director's Cut period is ten weeks.
On a long-form television motion picture of 91 minutes to two hours the Director's Cut period is 20 days, plus 5 days for each hour beyond two hours.
The producer must give the director five days' advance notice of the time and place of every preview of a theatrical film.
A director may ask for a preview of the Director's Cut before a public audience or, at the producer's choice, a private audience of no fewer than 100 people.

Under California's Program 4.0 a tax-credit project moves through five phases: application, documentation of the highest-ranked jobs ratios, the Credit Allocation Letter, principal photography through audit, and the Tax Credit Certificate.
value: Phase IV: principal photography to audit

facts.fact: A California tax-credit production must begin principal photography within 180 days of its Credit Allocation Letter, or 240 days if its qualified budget is $100 million or more.
A California tax-credit project must deliver its final element within 30 months of its Credit Allocation Letter.
SAG-AFTRA advises a low-budget producer to start the signatory process four to six weeks before using its performers, less under the Micro-Budget Agreement.
A City of Los Angeles film permit takes at least three full business days to process.
The DGA Low Budget Theatrical Sideletter covers scripted theatrical features budgeted up to $11 million, in seven levels from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
At DGA Low Budget Level 3 the director's salary is 33% of the Basic Agreement minimum with a 13-week guarantee, $108,168 in all.
A DGA low-budget employer must submit a Final Cost Statement to the DGA before principal photography begins.
The WGA Low Budget Agreement covers narrative theatrical features budgeted at or below $1.2 million, with a lower band from $500,000 to $1.2 million.
Under the WGA 2026 Basic Agreement a theatrical picture costing $5,000,000 or more is High Budget and one costing less is Low Budget, each with its own screenplay minimums.

Under the WGA 2026 Basic Agreement a dramatic SVOD program is High Budget if it costs $1,030,000 or more at 20 to 35 minutes, $1,750,000 or more at 36 to 65 minutes, or $3,000,000 or more at 66 minutes or longer; under 20 minutes it never is.

SAG-AFTRA's low-budget agreements cap the budget at $20,000 for Micro-Budget, $35,000 for Student Film, $50,000 for Short Project, $300,000 for Ultra Low Budget, $700,000 for Moderate Low Budget and $2,000,000 for Low Budget Theatrical.
Every SAG-AFTRA low-budget production must shoot entirely in the United States.
Under SAG-AFTRA's low-budget agreements there is no consecutive-day pay, except on overnight locations.
SAG-AFTRA may take a security deposit of 40% to 100% of covered performer payroll, returned at the completion of principal photography.
A production qualifies for California's Program 4.0 credit only with a budget of at least $1 million, or $1 million per episode for a new series of at least 20 minutes an episode.
The Academy counts a picture as feature length only if it runs over 40 minutes.
The Emmys count a half-hour episode as more than 20 and up to 40 minutes, and an hour-long episode as more than 40 minutes.

An animation, comedy, drama, variety, short-form or reality series needs six episodes premiered nationally in the Emmy year to enter as a series, and a documentary or hosted nonfiction series needs three.
Every episode of a limited or anthology series must premiere nationally by May 31 to compete that Emmy year.
Under the WGA's 2023 rules a development room has at least three writer-producers including the showrunner, guaranteed ten consecutive weeks.

A post-greenlight writers' room needs three writers for an order of 1 to 6 episodes, five for 7 to 12, and six for 13 or more, three of them writer-producers, guaranteed 20 weeks or the room's length if shorter.
A series written entirely by one writer or team is exempt from the WGA minimum-staffing rules.
The WGA minimum for writing a pilot is 150% of the episode minimum.
A Best Picture nomination goes to no more than three producers who did the major part of the producing.
To qualify for the 99th Academy Awards a feature must play for paid admission in a commercial theater in Los Angeles County, New York City, the Bay Area, Chicago, Dallas-Fort Worth or Atlanta.
The Academy's qualifying run is at least seven consecutive days in one theater with at least three screenings a day, one of them starting between 6 p.m. and 10 p.m.
A film first released in any non-theatrical medium is ineligible for the Oscars, though up to fifteen percent of its running time may be shown that way before the qualifying run.
For the 99th Academy Awards the qualifying run must begin between January 1 and December 31, 2026, and a picture gets only one qualifying run.
Films qualifying from July 1 to December 31, 2026 must file their Oscars submission forms by 5 p.m. PT on November 12, 2026.
A Best Picture contender also needs releases in nine more top-50 U.S. markets, ten in all, of at least seven days each with a daily showtime, within 45 days of the qualifying run.
Paramount committed at CinemaCon in April 2026 to a 45-day theatrical window and 90 days before subscription streaming, as reported quoting its CEO.
Universal's exclusive theatrical window reaches 45 days starting in 2027, as reported.
The global box office was $21.3 billion in 2021, by the MPA's 2021 THEME report, the latest it has published.
The U.S./Canada box office was $4.5 billion in 2021, on 470 million tickets sold.
In 2021, 47% of the U.S./Canada population, 168 million people, went to the cinema at least once.
Frequent moviegoers, who go once a month or more, were 3% of the U.S./Canada population in 2021 but bought 34% of tickets.
More than 940 films entered production worldwide during 2021.
Online video subscriptions worldwide reached 1.3 billion in 2021.
Sundance 2027 charged feature films $80 by July 27, $100 by August 28 and $125 by September 21, 2026, and shorts from $55.
A Sundance feature runs 50 minutes or more, and a U.S. feature must have at least half its financing from the United States.
Only films keeping world premiere status may enter Sundance's U.S. feature categories, and a film shown to the public before February 1, 2027 is ineligible.
The 2027 Sundance Film Festival runs January 21 to 31, 2027 in Boulder, Colorado.
A Cannes Official Selection film must have been produced in the twelve months before the festival, shown nowhere outside its home country, at no other international festival, and never online.
Every Cannes Competition film must be released commercially in French theatres.
Feature submissions for Cannes 2026 closed on March 13, 2026.
Rights-holders submitting to Cannes guarantee the film was made in compliance with health and safety law.
The Berlinale charges 175 euros to submit a feature and 75 euros for a short; features need at least 60 minutes and completion within 12 months of the festival.
Berlinale feature submissions for 2027 closed on October 21, 2026.
The Berlinale Competition takes world or international premieres only, and German films must be world premieres.
Venice 2026 took only world premieres completed after September 6, 2025, never shown publicly, to the press or online.
Venice 2026 charged 200 euros for a feature, rising to 250 euros from May 15, 2026.
SXSW 2027 charged features $95 by September 15 and $125 by October 1, 2026; the festival runs March 15 to 21, 2027 in Austin.
A screenplay or treatment of a future motion picture is not a fixation of the motion picture for copyright.
Offering a film for exhibition at a festival may count as publication.
Once a motion picture is published, its screenplay is published to the extent the film contains it.
A copyright owner cannot sue for infringement until the Copyright Office has acted on the registration.
Copyright registration costs $45 online for a single author's one work not made for hire, and $65 on the Standard Application.
Preregistering certain unpublished works costs $200.
Recording a transfer document costs $95 electronically or $125 on paper.
A work made for hire is protected for 95 years from first publication or 120 years from creation, whichever ends first; an individual's work since 1978 lasts the author's life plus 70 years.
A transfer of copyright ownership is valid only in a writing signed by the owner of the rights conveyed.
Between two conflicting transfers the first executed prevails if recorded within one month in the United States, or two months abroad.
WGA East script registration costs $10 for members, $17 for students and associates and $25 for the public, runs ten years, and gives no statutory protection.
Filming on location in the City of Los Angeles needs $1,000,000 of liability insurance, $500,000 for stills only and $2,000,000 for drones, naming the City and FilmLA as additional insured.
Filming in unincorporated Los Angeles County needs proof of workers' compensation and $1,000,000 of liability, or $5,000,000 with aircraft.
A City of Los Angeles film permit application costs $931 for up to five locations over seven consecutive days, and a simple student permit $52.
Standard filming hours in the City of Los Angeles are 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. on weekdays and 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. on weekends.
A program delivered to PBS needs errors and omissions insurance of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate, for at least three years, including title coverage.
California's Program 4.0 gives non-independent features and television a 35% credit on up to $120 million of qualified spending.
An independent film gets California's 35% credit on up to $20 million of qualified spending, and may sell or transfer the credit.
A series relocating to California gets a 40% credit for its first season there.
To qualify for California's credit at least 75% of the budget must be spent in California or at least 75% of principal photography days shot there.
California's Program 4.0 holds $3.75 billion over five years to June 30, 2030.
Live ammunition is never to be used on a set or brought onto any work location, under the industry's Safety Bulletin #1.
Firearms on a production are props in the charge of the Property Master, and only the Property Master and authorized cast should handle them.
Safety Bulletin #1 is to go out with the call sheet each day firearms or prop firearms are used.
The Industry Wide Labor-Management Safety Committee's bulletins are recommended guidelines, not law.
Before a minor performs a physical activity, the director, first assistant director, stunt coordinator and safety professional should confer with the minor, a parent and the studio teacher.
Every California employer must keep a written Injury and Illness Prevention Program.
In California a minor needs an Entertainment Work Permit to work in entertainment, valid for no more than six months.
In California a baby of 15 days to 6 months may be on set two hours and work twenty minutes.
In California a child of 6 months to 2 years may be on set four hours and work two.
In California a child of 2 to 6 may be on set six hours and work three.
In California a child of 6 to 9 may be on set eight hours, work four and have at least three hours of school when school is in session.
In California a minor of 9 to 16 may be on set nine hours, work five and have at least three hours of school when school is in session.
In California a minor of 16 to 18 may be on set ten hours, work six and have at least three hours of school when school is in session.
In California twelve hours must pass between a minor's dismissal and the next call.
A California production must provide a studio teacher for minors from 15 days to 16 years, one for every ten minors.
A parent or guardian must be with a California minor under 16 on set at all times.
Travel between studio and location counts toward a California minor's working day.
In New York a child performer needs a Child Performer Permit before work begins, and the employer needs a Certificate of Eligibility.
In New York an employer puts 15% of a child performer's gross earnings into a trust account.
In New York infants under 15 days old may not be employed, and child performers get 12 hours of rest between workdays.
In New York a child performer must get an average of at least three hours of instruction per school day, and never more than ten consecutive school days without it.
An R-rated film admits children under 17 only with a parent or adult guardian, and an NC-17 film admits no one 17 or under.
Nudity and sex scenes are not allowed under SAG-AFTRA's Micro-Budget Agreement.

Under SAG-AFTRA's first intimacy coordinator contract, ratified in December 2025, coordinators get minimum day and week rates, union health and pension, and access to performers' nudity and simulated sex riders.
The Academy's acting awards are four categories, actor and actress in a leading and in a supporting role, voted by the Actors Branch.
Only roles performed by humans with their consent are eligible for the Academy's acting awards.
The Emmys give separate lead actor and lead actress awards for series.

SAG-AFTRA's Moderate Low Budget and Low Budget agreements offer production incentives when half the speaking roles and days go to women, performers over 60, performers with disabilities or people of color, and 20% of days to people of color.

sources.title: The Hollywood Reporter: SAG-AFTRA National Board Unanimously Ratifies First Intimacy Coordinator Union Contract (December 19, 2025)
sources.said: The contract establishes minimum wage rates for daily and weekly work and inducts intimacy coordinators into the union health and pension plans. ... intimacy coordinators are additionally given access to material for their work including performers’ nudity/simulated sex riders and studio rules for such scenes.

sources.title: WGA: Showrunners’ Guide to 2023 MBA Writers’ Room Provisions
sources.said: These new minimum staffing provisions went into effect for seasons where the first episode is written on December 1, 2023 or after. ... Minimum staff: 3 writer-producers (including showrunner). ... Guarantee of 10 consecutive Weeks. ... Episode Order Required Writers Required Writer Producers 1 to 6 3 3 7-12 5* 3 13+ 6* 3 ... Minimum staff must be guaranteed 20 weeks or duration of the post-greenlight room, whichever is fewer. ... A show for which a single writer (including teams) is employed to write all episodes is exempt from the minimum staffing requirements.
